newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian oil industry welcomes native title plan.
newsitem.headline: Australian oil industry welcomes native title plan.

text.p: The Australian Petroleum Production and Exploration Association (APEA) said on Friday it welcomed the release by Prime Minister John Howard of his framework Ten Point plan for dealing with native title.

APEA's executive director Barry Jones said the framework plan was important, introduced greater transparency and focus into consultations with the government and set a clear structure within which future consultations could take place.
He said native title was a key issue for the petroleum industry, which had exploration and/or production titles over 18 percent of onshore Australia, much of this on pastoral leases.

The petroleum industry needed certainty of land title, efficient and effective processes for dealing with land titles and also sought to continue constructive and harmonious relations with Aboriginal communities, Jones said in a statement.
The industry did not seek or require the extinguishment of native title over pastoral leases in order to allow petroleum resources development to proceed.
This position was consistent with Howard's strong preference not to pursue a process that would result in wide-ranging extinguishment of native title, he said.
Some elements of the plan were particularly welcome, for example the undertaking to validate potentially invalid titles issues between January 1, 1994 and December 26, 1996, he said.
Other elements of the plan required further clarification and discussion, he said.
Australia's native title debate follows a judgement by the High Court in December last year, in a case involving the Wik tribe, that native title and pastoral leases could co-exist.
It had previously been broadly accepted that pastoral leases extinguished native title.
